evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test of Glyceryl Isostearate, the first challenge gave one positive reaction at 24 h and two at 48 h. evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal injections of 10% anisyl acetate with and without FCA, followed 1 week later by a 48 h occluded patch. Challenge: 24 h application of 5%, 10%, and 20% in acetone, 2 weeks after induction. Species: female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs (n=6). Reactions evaluated at 24 and 48 h after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: A guinea pig maximization test according to the Magnusson and Kligman (1969) method was conducted. Induction consisted of a series of six intradermal injections of 10% anisyl acetate with and without FCA followed one week later with a 48 h occluded patch. The guinea pigs were challenged two weeks later by a 24 h application of 5%, 10% and 20% in acetone. The application sites were left uncovered. Reactions were evaluated at 24 and 48 h after patch removal. There were no sensitization reactions in the six female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs (RIFM, 1983).

Challenge was performed with an occluded 24 h patch at 10% in petrolatum. The challenge concentration of 10% in petrolatum did not show any indications (0/10) of sensitization.

Challenge with undiluted and 50% test material produced no reactions at any site, indicating no evidence of a sensitization reaction in any test animal.

evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test, penicillin G was tested with intradermal induction at 3% w/v and topical induction at 5% w/v in 40% Tween 80, followed by topical challenge at 10% w/v. evidence.support_text: The second guinea pig maximization study used 0.025% amidoamine in intradermal injections and 1% amidoamine for topical induction, with two challenges. At the first challenge, 3 animals had a reaction score of at least 1, with 1 animal scoring 2. At the second challenge, 3 animals also had scores of at least 1. The study concluded that amidoamine was a moderate sensitizer.

evidence.support_text: In the first guinea pig maximization study, ten albino Dunkin/Hartley guinea pigs received intradermal injections of 0.1% amidoamine and topical induction with 5% amidoamine in acetone/PEG400. Challenge patches with 0.5% amidoamine were applied three times. At the first challenge, 7 animals had a reaction score of at least 0.5 at 24 hours, with 3 of 10 scoring 2. At the third challenge, all 10 guinea pigs had a score of at least 1, and 8 of 10 scored 2. The study concluded that amidoamine was a moderate sensitizer.

evidence.support_text: When the experiment was repeated using a 0.5-M induction concentration on day 0, 1 of 10 guinea pigs reacted after both the 21- and 35-day applications.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: albino guinea pig (Pirb-right white); Induction: 0.1 mL of 0.5% (v/v) dilution of CAPB (0.05% active) intradermal at two sites (with and without Freund complete adjuvant), plus 48-hour occlusive patch of 60% (v/v) dilution (6% active) one week later; Challenge: 24-hour occlusive patch of 10% (v/v) dilution (1% active) two weeks after induction; Vehicle: sterile isotonic saline for injections, distilled water for patches.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, 15 male Pirb-right white guinea pigs were induced intradermally with 0.5% (v/v) dilution of a commercial 10% active CAPB sample (0.05% active) and an occlusive patch of 60% (v/v) dilution (6% active), then challenged with 10% (v/v) dilution (1% active). No evidence of delayed contact hypersensitivity was found; the barely perceptible erythema in 2 test animals was attributed to adhesive bandages.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: albino guinea pigs (20 animals); Induction: 0.15% active CAPB; Challenge: 0.015% active CAPB; exact injection/patch volumes not repeated but same assay as previous.
evidence.support_text: The same laboratory tested 0.15% active CAPB for induction (0.015% for challenge) using the same maximization test. Slight erythema and edema were observed macroscopically in 6 of 20 test animals. Slight acanthosis was observed microscopically. Control animals had no dermatitis-type clinical or histological alterations.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: albino guinea pigs (20 animals); Induction: intradermal injections of 0.1% aqueous dilution of 30% active CAPB (0.03% active) with and without Freund complete adjuvant, plus 48-hour occlusive patch of 10% aqueous dilution (3% active) one week later; Challenge: 24-hour occlusive patch of 10% aqueous dilution (3% active) on left flank, water on right, 3 weeks after induction.
evidence.support_text: A full-strength 30% active CAPB sample was tested for skin sensitization using a maximization test in albino guinea pigs (20 animals). Induction: intradermal injections of 0.1% aqueous dilution (0.03% active) and 48-hour occlusive patch of 10% aqueous dilution (3% active). Challenge: 24-hour occlusive patch of 10% aqueous dilution (3% active) on left flank, water on right. At necropsy, 8 of 20 test animals exhibited erythema and edema, with microscopic findings of epidermal acanthosis, inter- and intracellular edema, and lymphomonocytic infiltration with eosinophils in superficial dermis. The investigators concluded that the commercial CAPB is capable of producing delayed-type contact sensitization.
